text.p: SME - Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar said he did not consider exclusion of Slovakia from the first wave of NATO enlargement as a failure of his governemnt. Meciar said he was not dissapointed with the NATO decision, saying the alliance has signalled it would make such a move over the past year.

- U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright on Wednesday expressed her concern over several issues which still remain unsolved in Slovakia. During a brief meeting with Meciar, Albright pointed mainly to the death of a former policeman linked to the kidnapping of president's son, the abduction itself, the minority language law and freedom of the press.
- Ruling coalition deputies on Wednesday outvoted the opposition and rejected its demand that Meciar present a statement to parliament on why Slovakia was not included in NATO enlargement plans.
- Parliament on Wednesday approved a law on wage regulations.
- Opposition parties in the left-wing coalition Spolocna Volba (The Common Choice) on Wednesday agreed to disband the coalition this year.

- The Slovak Jewish community and the Czech National Bank have agreed that gold belonging to Slovak Jews before the Holocaust would be trasferred to a foundation called Fond Podpory which will use the funds for charity.
NARODNA OBRODA - The Slovak government is planning a new law to lower direct and increase indirect taxes, including an increase in the value added tax.
- Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) Chairman Marian Sasik said only about one-tenth of the 900 issues listed on the BSE were liquid, adding investors had no interest in the rest of the shares.
- The opposition Party of the Democratic Left (SDL) has worked out an amendment to an election law which it wants to present to parliament in September.
PRAVDA - Parliament will hold its next regular session from August 20.
